conflicts.point: Whether mandatory pre-release safety testing under the Export Administration Regulations provides effective containment for frontier artificial intelligence models.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-release evaluation creates enforceable legal constraints that successfully contain safety risks before deployment.
Pre-release testing mandates fail because algorithmic optimizations and open-source diffusion outpace regulatory review cycles.

conflicts.point: Whether regulatory focus should prioritize border-based software export controls or domestic structural interventions such as revenue levies and worker retraining.

positions.stance: Preventing unaligned model scaling and catastrophic risks takes priority over domestic economic redistribution.
Export control compliance is an administrative shield that ignores labor displacement and resource extraction; domestic utility levies are necessary.

verdicts.conflict: Whether mandatory pre-release safety testing under the Export Administration Regulations provides effective containment for frontier artificial intelligence models.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position under C2 names concrete regulatory instruments like the Export Administration Regulations and requires auditable safety proofs, whereas the accelerationist position relies on abstract assertions about algorithmic optimization without detailing alternative enforcement mechanisms.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical documentation showing that open-source diffusion successfully bypasses mandatory pre-release testing at scale would flip this verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether regulatory focus should prioritize border-based software export controls or domestic structural interventions such as revenue levies and worker retraining.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position directly addresses transnational security risks tied to frontier AI scaling, whereas the skeptic position under C5 abandons export controls entirely to focus on domestic taxation, ignoring the international security dimensions of unconstrained model proliferation.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence proving that international export controls are completely unenforceable and that domestic taxation is the sole viable regulatory lever would alter this balance.
